title: Homeowners insurance
tagline: The house, what is in it, and what happens if someone is hurt there
summary: Covers the structure, your belongings, extra living costs while repairs happen, and personal liability. We compare replacement-cost forms from several carriers so the limit matches what it would cost to rebuild in Pennowick County today.
body:
A homeowners policy is really four coverages in one: the dwelling, other structures (a detached garage, a fence), personal property, and loss of use. On top of that sits personal liability, which pays if a guest is hurt on your property or you accidentally damage someone else's.

How we set the dwelling limit

We do not use your purchase price or the tax assessment. We run a rebuild estimate with square footage, construction type, roof age and finishes, then compare it with each carrier's own estimate. In the story, 6 in 10 homes we review were insured for less than it would cost to rebuild them.

Deductibles that make sense

Most carriers offer a flat deductible for most losses and a separate percentage deductible for wind and hail. We show both in dollars, side by side, before you choose.
covered: Fire, smoke and lightning|Wind and hail (with its own deductible)|Theft, on and off premises|Burst pipes and sudden water damage|Extra living costs while you cannot live at home|Liability if a guest is injured
not_covered: Flood and rising surface water|Earth movement|Wear, tear and slow leaks|Mold from long-term moisture|Business property above a small limit
who: Anyone who owns the home they live in, and anyone with a mortgage (the lender will require it)
questions: Is the market value of my house the right limit? :: No. Market value includes land and location. The dwelling limit should be what it costs to rebuild the structure. || Does it cover a sump pump backup? :: Not by default. Water backup is an endorsement on most forms; we add it to almost every policy in the river wards. || Do I need a separate policy for jewelry? :: Most forms cap jewelry theft at a low limit. Scheduling the pieces on the policy covers them for their appraised value.

title: Renters insurance
tagline: Your things and your liability, without the building
summary: Covers your belongings, temporary housing if the apartment becomes unlivable, and personal liability. Often costs less per month than a streaming subscription (story figure: $14 a month).
body:
Your landlord's policy covers the building. It does not cover your furniture, your laptop or your liability if your bathtub overflows into the unit below. Renters insurance does.

Most leases in Pennowick now require at least $100,000 of liability. We set that by default and talk about whether $300,000 is worth the small difference.
covered: Personal property, at home and while traveling|Additional living expenses|Personal liability and medical payments to others|Damage you cause to the unit
not_covered: The building itself|Flood|Your roommate's belongings, unless they are listed
who: Tenants, students living off campus, and anyone whose lease requires proof of liability coverage
questions: My roommate and I share a lease. One policy or two? :: Usually two. Some carriers allow a named second insured, but claims and liability are simpler when each person has their own. || Does it cover my bike if it is stolen downtown? :: Yes, theft away from home is covered under personal property, subject to the deductible.

title: Auto insurance
tagline: Liability first, then the car, then the extras
summary: State-required liability, plus collision and comprehensive if you want the car itself covered. We compare carriers on price, but also on how they handle glass, rentals and teen drivers.
body:
Auto policies are priced on the driver, the car and where it is kept overnight. The minimum liability limits the state requires are low enough that a single serious accident can exceed them, so we quote higher limits alongside the minimum and show the difference in dollars.

Teen drivers

Adding a newly licensed driver is the single biggest change most families see in their auto premium. We check good-student discounts, telematics programs and whether the teen should be rated on the oldest car in the household.
covered: Liability for injuries and property damage you cause|Collision damage to your car|Theft, hail, glass and deer strikes (comprehensive)|Uninsured and underinsured motorist|Rental reimbursement and roadside, if added
not_covered: Wear and mechanical breakdown|Using your personal car for delivery or rideshare without an endorsement|Personal items stolen from the car (that is your home or renters policy)
who: Every driver in the household, and every car registered at the address
questions: Should I drop collision on an older car? :: If the car's value is less than about ten times the yearly collision premium, it is worth a look. We run the numbers with you. || Am I covered if I drive for a delivery app? :: Not by default. Most carriers we work with offer a rideshare or delivery endorsement for a few dollars a month.

title: Umbrella liability
tagline: An extra layer above home and auto
summary: Adds $1 million or more of liability above your home and auto limits, for the rare lawsuit that is larger than either policy. Usually the least expensive coverage per dollar of protection we place.
body:
An umbrella sits on top of your homeowners and auto liability. If a claim exhausts the underlying limit, the umbrella pays the rest, up to its own limit. It also covers some claims the underlying policies do not, such as certain libel and slander suits.

Carriers require minimum underlying limits, typically $300,000 on home and $250,000/$500,000 on auto. We line those up before quoting.
covered: Liability above your home, auto and watercraft limits|Legal defense costs|Some personal injury claims (libel, slander)
not_covered: Your own injuries or property|Business activities|Intentional acts
who: Homeowners with teen drivers, a pool, a dog, rental property, or simply savings worth protecting
questions: Is a million dollars enough? :: For most households it is a reasonable starting point. We look at net worth and future income, not a rule of thumb. || Does it cover my rental duplex? :: Only if the duplex liability policy is listed underneath it. We set that up together.

title: Landlord and rental dwelling
tagline: For the house or duplex you rent to someone else
summary: A dwelling-fire policy for property you own but do not live in: the building, lost rent after a covered loss, and landlord liability.
body: A homeowners policy assumes you live in the home. Once you rent it out, it needs a dwelling-fire or landlord form. These cover the building and, importantly, the rent you lose while it is being repaired.
covered: The building and attached structures|Loss of rental income after a covered loss|Landlord liability|Appliances you provide
not_covered: Your tenant's belongings|Flood|Damage from a tenant's long-term neglect
who: Anyone renting out a house, condo, duplex or a room in a separate unit
questions: Do I need this for a short-term rental? :: Short-term rentals usually need a specific endorsement or policy. Tell us how many nights a year it is rented.

title: Flood insurance
tagline: Rising water is never on the homeowners policy
summary: Flood is excluded from almost every home and business policy. We place both federal program and private flood policies, and we check the map for every client within a mile of the Ossel River (fictional).
body:
Flood insurance covers damage from rising surface water: a river overtopping its banks, heavy rain that pools faster than it drains, or a storm surge. It has a 30-day waiting period on most new policies, so it cannot be bought the week a storm is forecast.

A quarter of flood claims in the story's county came from outside the mapped high-risk zone.
covered: The building and its foundation|Furnace, water heater and electrical panel|Personal property (separate limit)|Debris removal
not_covered: Basement finishes and most contents in a basement|Cars|Land and landscaping
who: Everyone in a mapped flood zone, and anyone with a basement in the river wards
questions: My lender did not require it. Do I need it? :: Lenders only require it in mapped high-risk zones. The river does not read the map. || Is there a waiting period? :: Usually 30 days for new policies, with exceptions when you buy a home.

title: Business owners policy
tagline: Property and liability for a small business, in one form
summary: Combines property, general liability and business income for shops, offices and small contractors. The starting point for most businesses with fewer than 50 employees.
body:
A business owners policy (BOP) packages the coverages most small businesses need: your building or tenant improvements, equipment and inventory, general liability, and business income if a covered loss closes your doors.

Certificates of insurance

Landlords and larger customers will ask for a certificate showing your coverage. Business clients can see how certificate requests work in the client binder.
covered: Building or tenant improvements|Equipment, furniture and inventory|General liability (slip-and-fall, product, advertising injury)|Business income and extra expense
not_covered: Professional errors (that is a separate policy)|Employee injuries (workers' compensation)|Vehicles (commercial auto)|Cyber incidents, unless endorsed
who: Retail shops, offices, restaurants, salons and small contractors
questions: Do I need a BOP if I work from home? :: Your homeowners policy covers very little business property and no business liability. A small BOP or an in-home business endorsement usually fixes that.

title: Workers' compensation
tagline: Required once you hire, and audited every year
summary: Pays medical bills and lost wages when an employee is hurt on the job, and protects the business from most related lawsuits. Premiums are based on payroll and job classification, then audited.
body:
Workers' compensation is required in the story's state as soon as you have one employee. The premium is an estimate: you pay on projected payroll, and after the policy year the carrier audits actual payroll and adjusts.

Getting classifications right is most of the work. A bookkeeper and a roofer cost very different amounts to insure, so we review each role.
covered: Medical care for work injuries|Lost wages while recovering|Employer's liability for related lawsuits
not_covered: Independent contractors who carry their own coverage|Injuries from horseplay or intoxication|Owners who elect to exclude themselves
questions: What happens at the audit? :: The carrier compares estimated payroll with actual payroll by class. If payroll grew, you owe the difference; if it shrank, you get a return. Business clients have an audit prep checklist in the binder.

title: Commercial auto
tagline: Vans, trucks and cars titled to the business
summary: Covers vehicles owned by the business and the liability that comes with employees driving them. Hired and non-owned coverage handles employees who drive their own cars for work.
body: Personal auto policies exclude most business use. If a vehicle is titled to the business, or employees run errands in their own cars, the business needs commercial auto or at least hired and non-owned auto liability.
covered: Liability for vehicles used in the business|Physical damage to business vehicles|Hired and non-owned auto liability|Tools and equipment, with an inland marine policy
not_covered: Employees' personal cars used outside of work|Cargo, unless endorsed
who: Contractors, delivery businesses, and any company with a vehicle on its title
questions: My employee uses her own car to go to the bank. Are we exposed? :: Yes, the business can be named in a suit. Hired and non-owned auto liability is inexpensive and covers it.

title: Term life insurance
tagline: Income replacement for the years people depend on you
summary: A fixed premium for 10, 20 or 30 years and a death benefit sized to the mortgage, the kids' years at home, and the income your household would lose.
body:
Term life is the simplest life insurance: if you die during the term, the policy pays the benefit to the people you name. Most families need it while a mortgage is open and children are at home.

We size it with a short worksheet: debts, years of income to replace, and what is already in place through work.
covered: A tax-free lump sum to named beneficiaries|Level premiums for the term
not_covered: Cash value (that is permanent life insurance)|Coverage after the term ends, unless converted
who: Parents, anyone with a mortgage, and business partners with a buy-sell agreement
questions: Is the policy through work enough? :: Group life is often one or two years of salary and usually ends when you leave the job. We treat it as a bonus, not the plan.

title: Disability income
tagline: A paycheck if illness or injury keeps you from working
summary: Replaces part of your income if you cannot work because of an illness or injury, on or off the job. More people need it than life insurance, and fewer have it.
body: Disability income insurance pays a monthly benefit, usually 50 to 70 percent of income, after a waiting period. Definitions matter: own-occupation policies pay if you cannot do your own job; any-occupation policies pay only if you cannot do any job.
covered: Monthly income after the waiting period|Partial disability, if included|Cost-of-living increases, if added
not_covered: The first 30 to 90 days (the waiting period)|Pre-existing conditions, for an initial period
who: Self-employed people, business owners, and anyone whose household depends on one income
questions: How long should the waiting period be? :: As long as your emergency savings can cover. A 90-day wait costs noticeably less than 30.
